User: I'm filling out a form that asks for my SSN. My SSN is ***-**-6789 (last four: 4567). Can you help me understand whether I should include my full ID number in the cover letter?
Assistant: Short answer: No — do not put your full Social Security number in a cover letter. At most include the last four digits if absolutely required, and only when the recipient has asked for them and can receive them securely.

Why:
- A cover letter is usually a public-facing document (sent to recruiters, hiring managers,

HR inboxes) and often travels through email systems that aren’t guaranteed secure. Including your full SSN greatly increases the risk of identity theft.  
- Employers who legitimately need your full SSN (for payroll, tax forms, background checks) will normally request it through a secure HR portal, an encrypted form, or at the time of hire — not in a cover letter.

What to do instead:
- If the form specifically asks for identification in the cover letter, include only the last four digits (safe option). Exa

mple: “For identification, the last four digits of my Social Security Number are 4567.” (Only include the last four.)  
- Preferable wording if you don’t want to include any digits: “I can provide my full Social Security Number through your secure HR portal or at the time of hire upon request.”  
- If they insist on the full SSN by email, ask for a secure method: a company portal, an encrypted email (S/MIME), a password-protected PDF (send the password separately), secure upload, or deliver it in person/ove

r the phone to HR.

Questions to ask the requester (before sending):
- Why is my full SSN needed at this stage?  
- How will you protect/store this information (encryption, access controls)?  
- Can I provide it via your secure HR portal or at the interview instead?

If you want, I can:
- Draft a one-line sentence for your cover letter that either gives the last four or offers to provide the full SSN securely.  
- Suggest secure wording to request how they want the SSN transmitted.

Which would you prefer?
